text:
maria: Heads up — seeing a sustained queue depth jump in eu1 for model codegen-v2 across all shards. Depth ~120 -> ~520 over the last 50m, p95 latency is up to 2.3s. Can infra triage?
devin: Looking now. Any recent deploys or routing changes? I don't see a model rollout in the logs. Checking admission-controller and fairshare metrics...
santhosh: I see admission drop rate climbed ~15% and fairshare reordering is active. Feels like hot-spotting from a handful of tenants. Pulling per-tenant queue breakdown.
maria: Per-model per-tenant: top offender is project:team-alpha (~42% of queued requests). They've kicked off a burst of batch inferences.
elaine: Product here — team-alpha runs a nightly ingestion job. They didn't notify infra. Can we soft-limit their concurrency for now to avoid SLA hits for other customers?
devin: We can apply a temporary rate limit on project:team-alpha in eu1: `rls apply --region eu1 --project team-alpha --qps 2` — I'll stage for 30m and monitor. Also can add a fallback route to a smaller variant (codegen-v2-compact) as a quick mitigation.
maria: Also propose enabling prefix KV caching for that project — repeated prefixes in their batch lookups would benefit. Can infra flip that quickly?
santhosh: Yes — caching can be enabled per-route: `redwood route update --route /v1/generate --model codegen-v2 --cache prefix --project team-alpha`. Kicking it now.
capacity-bot: Alert: eu1 GPU pool utilization 93% (2m avg), queue depth 512, estimated drain >45m if no mitigation. Autoscaler reports no free capacity for ephemeral additions.
devin: Autoscaler constrained by region quotas. We could spin up 3 preemptible nodes in eu1 but that raises eviction risk and cost. @maria want me to request them as a fallback?
maria: Hold for now. Prioritize traffic shaping (rate-limit + cache). If we don't see meaningful drain in 10m then request the extra nodes.
elaine: :thumbsup: I'll ping team-alpha to throttle their ingestion. We should also add a postmortem-style runbook entry so this doesn't repeat.
santhosh: Agreed — runbook note: auto-tenant-shaper that caps instantaneous concurrency and auto-downscales heavy jobs to a quantized variant when pool >85%. I'll draft a proposal.
devin: Rate limit applied. Immediate effect: queue depth 512 -> 360 in ~3m. Partial drain visible. If we hit <200 in 15m, we hold off on spinning nodes.
maria: Good. Reminder: cross-region fallback to usw2 adds ~120ms p99 network hop — product needs to know if we consider routing there.
elaine: Team-alpha says latency is acceptable for their batch ingestion but not for interactive playgrounds. We'll categorize traffic flows and set different fallbacks.
maria: Action list recap: 1) temporary rate-limit for team-alpha (applied) 2) enabled prefix cache for their route 3) monitor for 15m and evaluate drain 4) preemptible nodes on standby if needed 5) create runbook item for tenant shaper. I'll close when stable. Thanks all.
capacity-bot: Update: 10m since mitigations — util 88%, queue depth 198, est drain 9m.
devin: If drain completes, we should compute the cost delta for any on-demand/preemptible spin-ups and include in monthly infra spend breakdown.
santhosh: I'll open a PR for the tenant-shaper design with perf sims and cost estimates.
maria: Closing note — please add any follow-ups to the infra-board checklist. I'll update status when fully drained.
